body:
ADR-0023 moves everything OS-specific into `targets/<id>/`. Nothing creates the folder or loads it yet, and the gate (#12) needs its allowlist from there.

- Create `targets/ubuntu-26.04/` with `target.toml` (id, display name, os-release match, shell `bash`, package-owner query `dpkg -S`, sudo implementation and version) and `allowlist.toml` holding the v1 entries from spec `policy-gate/v1` §6.4. The other files (`model.toml`, `gate-vectors.toml`, `prompts/`, `harvest.toml`, `eval/`) are added by the issues that first need them.
- At start-up, read `/etc/os-release` and pick the target whose `ID` and `VERSION_ID` match exactly. No fallback via `ID_LIKE` or a nearby version.
- With no match, say so and start only if the user names a target (`--target <id>` or `target =` in `config.toml`, ADR-0020).
- A named target that does not match the OS puts the gate in degraded mode (spec `policy-gate/v1` §7.7). `:status` shows the active target and whether it matches.
- Code outside `targets/` must not name an OS.

**Done when:** tests (under the temporary HOME, #73) cover an exact match, no match without `--target`, a mismatched `--target` (degraded), and a target with a missing or malformed `target.toml` (refused with a message).

Implements ADR-0023 (Proposed; builds against it per #95). Blocks the allowlist loading in #12.
title: M0.15 — Target folder for ubuntu-26.04 and target selection at start-up
